name: Sporadic Fetal Brain Disruption Sequence

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Fetal Brain Disruption Sequence

criteria.description: Severe microcephaly with normal head circumference in early gestation followed by progressive brain volume loss
Characteristic craniofacial abnormalities including prominent occiput and sloping forehead
Presence of intracranial calcifications on prenatal or postnatal imaging
Normal chromosomal analysis excluding other genetic syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe microcephaly with characteristic craniofacial abnormalities plus exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and exclusion of genetic etiologies

laboratory: Exclusion of infectious etiologies by serology
imaging: Prenatal or postnatal MRI showing severe brain volume loss
Intracranial calcifications on CT or ultrasound
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Exclusion of congenital infections such as TORCH

distinguishingFeatures: History of maternal Zika virus exposure
Positive Zika virus serology or PCR
Additional systemic involvement such as arthrogryposis
Positive maternal or neonatal serology for TORCH infections
Presence of systemic signs such as hepatosplenomegaly

redFlags: Severe microcephaly detected prenatally or at birth
references: Orphanet: Sporadic Fetal Brain Disruption Sequence - ORPHA:1665
Pagon RA, et al. GeneReviews: Microcephaly. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
Moore CA, et al. Fetal brain disruption sequence: clinical and neuropathologic findings. Am J Med Genet. 1990.
